## What to Look for in FP&A Software for Life Sciences Companies


Life sciences FP&A software must support R&D-centric budgeting, milestone-driven forecasting, and runway modeling that reflects the probabilistic nature of drug development. Generic financial planning tools lack the structural flexibility to handle these requirements without extensive customization.


When evaluating platforms, prioritize capabilities that map directly to how biotech and pharma companies actually operate. Clinical trial costs represent the largest budget category for most life sciences organizations, and these costs behave differently than typical operating expenses. They fluctuate based on patient enrollment rates, site activation timelines, and CRO contract structures that include pass-through costs and fee-for-service components.


The ability to model scenarios based on clinical milestones is essential. Your platform should allow you to build forecasts that adjust automatically when a program advances from Phase 1 to Phase 2, or when enrollment targets shift. This milestone-based approach differs fundamentally from the calendar-driven budgeting that works for other industries.


Integration capabilities matter significantly for life sciences finance teams. Your FP&A platform should connect with your ERP, clinical trial management systems, and cap table software to create a unified view of financial performance. Grant accounting represents another critical requirement for many biotech companies. Platforms must support the tracking and reporting requirements associated with NIH grants, BARDA contracts, and other government funding sources that come with specific compliance obligations.

The domains of life sciences finance (clinical development, regulatory affairs, manufacturing scale-up) each introduce planning variables that generic platforms treat as afterthoughts rather than core functionality.

## How Platforms Handle R&D Budget Modeling and Clinical Trial Costs


Platforms handle R&D budget modeling through driver-based approaches that connect clinical assumptions to financial outcomes, allowing finance teams to model costs based on enrollment rates, site counts, and protocol complexity rather than simple line-item projections.


Clinical trial budgeting represents the most complex area of life sciences financial planning. A single Phase 3 trial can span multiple years, involve dozens of clinical sites across different countries, and include cost categories ranging from investigator fees to central lab services to patient travel reimbursements. Effective platforms structure these costs in ways that reflect how they actually accrue.


CRO cost tracking requires particular attention. Contract research organizations typically bill through a combination of fixed fees, unit-based charges, and pass-through costs. Your FP&A platform should model each component separately, allowing you to forecast how changes in enrollment pace or protocol amendments affect total program costs.


The life cycle of a clinical program introduces planning challenges at each phase transition. Moving from Phase 2 to Phase 3 typically increases costs substantially, and platforms must support the scenario modeling needed to understand how different development paths affect overall R&D spend and company runway.


Probability weighting adds another layer of complexity. Not every program in your pipeline will succeed, and sophisticated financial planning requires adjusting expected costs and timelines based on historical success rates for each clinical phase. Platforms that support probability-weighted forecasting help finance teams present more realistic projections to investors and board members.

## Burn Rate Forecasting and Runway Planning for Investor Reporting


Burn rate forecasting and runway planning require platforms that can model multiple scenarios simultaneously and present results in formats that satisfy investor and board reporting requirements. The best platforms automate the connection between operational assumptions and cash runway calculations.


For biotech companies, burn rate is not a static metric. It fluctuates based on clinical trial activity, hiring plans, and the timing of major vendor payments. Effective FP&A platforms model burn rate dynamically, showing how changes in any input variable cascade through to runway projections.


Investor reporting demands specific outputs. Board members and investors expect to see runway under multiple scenarios: typically a base case, an upside case reflecting faster-than-expected progress, and a downside case accounting for delays or setbacks. Platforms should generate these scenarios without requiring finance teams to maintain separate models for each.


The connection between clinical milestones and financing events adds strategic importance to runway planning. Many biotech companies time their fundraising around data readouts or regulatory submissions, and FP&A platforms must support the what-if analysis needed to understand how different milestone timelines affect financing requirements.


Cash runway calculations for life sciences companies must account for the lumpy nature of R&D spending. Unlike SaaS companies with relatively predictable monthly burn, biotech companies experience significant month-to-month variation based on clinical trial enrollment, manufacturing campaigns, and regulatory submission timelines.

## How to Match a Platform to Your Life Sciences Planning Complexity


Match the platform to your planning structure. Teams with one or two clinical programs usually need quick setup and clear runway reporting. Teams with several programs at different phases need milestone-linked scenarios, probability-weighted forecasts and board reporting. Organizations with portfolios across therapeutic areas need interconnected models and cross-program analysis. For each shortlisted vendor, confirm which of these structures it supports, and ask for a clear implementation plan with named owners and milestones.
